items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1959-06-30
items.q: especially cats like Willigan's on drums, Lee Collins on, on Corny, Ernest Keller on trombone

ctx.x: And he played the beat at the drum?

He played the drum. I didn't know a lot of guys. But they were very annoyed at us when we come to Pensacola. We worked for Nick the Greeks there, at his cafeteria upstairs. And we were somewhat of a sensation in Pensacola. Those people starved for real organized bands, especially cats like Willigan's on drums, Lee Collins on, on Corny, Ernest Keller on trombone, Arthur Durden and Lee Rousin on saxophone. It was really, you know, something that was like, a real, real, real great sounding band at that time, you…
I wonder if we could get the name of some of the different guys in your Boozang, King, Boozang,

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Lee Collins and Ernest Kelly before David Jones. Went . . . played like 20 one- nighters

ctx.x: In the late ’20s, around 1928, you also did a little touring with David Jones and Lee Collins?

Lee Collins and Ernest Kelly before David Jones. Went . . . played like 20 one- nighters, and every one of them was a baza, which means it’s a bust-out, was nothing. They tell you, “You should have come here Thursday.” Thursday was payday. You come here on Saturday and Sunday or Monday, ain’t nobody. Nobody got no money. They spend up all their money. You mentioned David Jones, you mention a real giant. You never hear his name, but he was a real giant. He played tenor saxophone, played clarinet. His main forte…
